newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Valecom closes deal with Japanese in CVRD bid.
newsitem.headline: Valecom closes deal with Japanese in CVRD bid.

text.p: A group of 12 Japanese steelmakers and trading firms led by Nippon Steel Corp has signed an agreement to join the Valecom consortium to bid in the privatization auction of Brazilian state mining giant CVRD, Valecom said in a statement.

The Valecom consortium is being led by Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim and South Africa's Anglo-American Corp which have equal stakes in the consortium amounting to more than 50 percent jointly.

The group of Japanese investors will have a 10 percent stake in Valecom. It includes Nippon Steel Corp, NKK Corp, Kawasaki Steel Corp, Sumitomo Metal Industries Ltd, Kobe Steel Ltd, Nisshin Steel Co Ltd, Nakayama Steel Works Ltd, Nissho Iwai Corp, Mitsui & Co Ltd, Mitsubishi Corp, Itochu Corp and Marubeni Corp.

"We very much welcome the participation of the Japanese consortium in the Valecom Association and believe that the working experience that its members have in the steel and iron ore industries will be beneficial to the further development of CVRD as one of the pre-eminent iron ore producers in the world," Valecom said in the statement.

It said Valecom was also holding talks with other investors, including CVRD's employees who can acquire 4.45 percent of CVRD voting shares under the privatization rules and plan to join whichever consortium wins after the auction.
Valecom, one of two consortia planning to bid at the privatization auction, also includes two Brazilian pension funds, Centrus and Sistel, which already have a joint stake of 2.8 percent in CVRD.

The other consortium is being led by Brazilian steelmaker CSN and includes Nations Bank, Opportunity Asset Management, South Africa's Gencor and four Brazilian pension funds, Previ, Petros, Funcef and Funcesp.
The four pension funds already have a joint voting stake of around 10.03 percent in CVRD which would give the CSN consortium a controlling position in CVRD if it wins the auction.
CSN is also holding talks with Brazilian pulp and paper group Suzano, construction firm Camargo Correia and U.S. aluminium company Alcoa.
A 40-45 percent voting stake in CVRD is being sold off April 29 on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange for a minimum price of 3 billion reais ($2.83 billion).
